title: Workflow canvas — access, change & vendor playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines an integrated, cross-functional lifecycle for common operational flows at Redwood Inference: access and permissions requests, change management for production services, data handling classification and approvals, procurement and expense approvals, vendor onboarding, and travel & expense templates. The goal is to reduce friction for employees while maintaining predictable controls, auditability, and clear escalation paths.

Audience:
- People managers requesting access or purchases
- Engineers deploying changes to production
- Finance staff processing invoices/expenses
- Security and Legal reviewers
- Vendor managers and procurement contacts

Ownership and governance:
- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team)
- Control partners: Security, Eng SRE, People Ops
- Operational steward (day-to-day): Procurement Specialist (procurement@redwood.com)
- Review cadence: annual policy review, or after any incident that affects controls

Key principles:
1) Least privilege: default access must be scoped to minimal roles and temporary where possible.
2) Separation of duties: procurement approvals must be independent from requesters.
3) Risk-based review: high-impact data or spend requires Security/Legal sign-off.
4) Auditability: every access, change, and vendor payment must have a recorded approval trail.

Section 1 — Access & permissions lifecycle
Purpose: Standardize how employees request, approve, and obtain access to systems, datasets, and cloud resources.

Process summary (high level):
1. Request: Employee files an Access Request via the internal portal (Forms → Access Requests) including justification, duration, and owner.
2. Manager approval: Requesting manager validates business need and verifies the duration.
3. Control review: Security reviews requests for dataset or infra access (if resource labeled "sensitive" or environment == production).
4. Provisioning: IAM or CloudOps automates role assignment; ephemeral sessions preferred.
5. Post-provision review: Quarterly entitlement review triggers periodic recertification.

Request template required fields (portal):
- Requester name and email
- Manager name
- Resource(s) requested (clear ARNs or dataset ids)
- Role(s) requested (e.g., viewer, editor, deployer)
- Business justification (what the access enables)
- Duration request (end date for temporary access)
- Attach related change ticket ID (if applicable)

Automated RBAC example (CLI snippet):
- Grant: rbactool grant --user maya.chen --role viewer --resource dataset:prod/customer-embeddings --expires 2026-07-31
- Revoke: rbactool revoke --user maya.chen --resource dataset:prod/customer-embeddings

Entitlement review cadence:
- Production infra & sensitive datasets: quarterly recertification by owner
- Non-sensitive dev/test resources: semi-annual

Escalation matrix (access issues):
- No access after approval: raise ticket to CloudOps (sla 4 business hours)
- Unexpected high-privilege grant: Auto-block and notify Security (SLA 1 hour)

Section 2 — Change management (services & infra)
Goal: Ensure safe, observable rollouts with rollback plans and defined owners. Applies to infra, runtime, and model-serving configurations.

Change categories:
- Standard change: pre-authorized repeatable changes (e.g., routine config updates). Require change ticket, owner, and monitoring plan. No CAB required.
- Major change: changes that affect production availability, data integrity, or security posture (e.g., kernel upgrades, model compilation changes). Require formal CAB review and test plan.
- Emergency change: when active incident requires immediate action. Must be documented post-hoc and retro-reviewed within 72 hours.

Minimum change ticket fields:
- Change ID and title
- Owner and rollback owner
- Scope and affected services (list services and environments)
- Risk assessment (low/medium/high) and impact statement
- Test plan and validation queries (what to monitor)
- Rollback procedure with exact commands and expected outcomes
- Scheduled window and expected downtime (if any)

Approval matrix:
- Low risk: Owner + Manager signoff
- Medium risk: Owner + Manager + Eng SRE review
- High risk: CAB approval (includes Security and Product)

Deployment checklist (pre-deploy):
1. Run unit and integration tests (all green)
2. Canary in a non-prod region for min 1 hour with traffic reproduction
3. Instrumented metrics and alerts configured (latency, error rate, token throughput)
4. Communication: notify oncall, affected teams, and change channel
5. Backup/restore snapshot verified (where applicable)

Section 3 — Data management & classification
Purpose: Define handling rules for different data classifications and required controls.

Classification tiers and handling summary:
- Public: No restrictions; can be shared externally.
- Internal: Default classification; internal use only.
- Confidential: Customer data, business-sensitive metrics — requires encryption at rest and in transit, access controls, and logging.
- Restricted: Regulated or high-risk (PII, health, financial). Requires Legal and Security approval for storage, transfer, and processing.

Required controls by classification (table):
"Classification | Storage | Access | Audit | Data Masking
Public | Any | N/A | Optional | No
Internal | Encrypted recommended | Role-based | Periodic | No
Confidential | Encrypted (KMS) | RBAC + approval | Audit logs required | Partial or tokenization recommended
Restricted | Encrypted (HSM where applicable) | Limited list + Justification | Immutable audit trail | Strong masking or pseudonymization"

Handling rules and approvals:
- Any dataset labeled "Restricted" requires Security + Legal sign-off before creation.
- ETL or exports containing Confidential or Restricted fields must be approved via Data Access Request and logged.
- Data retention: follow retention schedule published in Data Retention Matrix (referenced doc id in related_pages).

Section 4 — Procurement, expenses, and vendor management
Purpose: Provide a single decision canvas for approvals, thresholds, and vendor onboarding steps.

Procurement thresholds and approvals (table):
"Amount (USD) | Approval required | Notes
<$2,000 | Manager | Office supplies, routine SaaS seats
$2,000–$25,000 | Manager + Procurement Specialist | Standard vendor contract; PO required
$25,001–$250,000 | Director Finance + Legal review | Includes vendor risk assessment
>$250,000 | VP/Exec + Legal + Security | Board-notified for multi-year commitments or strategic vendor"

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Initial request and business justification (owner submits vendor form)
2. Procurement collects quotes and performs cost comparison
3. Security runs vendor risk assessment (connectivity, data access, subprocessor list)
4. Legal reviews contract & SLA; include data processing addendum if applicable
5. Finance issues PO and routes invoice processing
6. Ops/IT provisioning and logging configuration
7. Quarterly vendor performance review for strategic vendors

Payment and invoice guidance:
- Standard net terms are net-30 unless negotiated.
- All invoices must cite PO number and matched to contract in procurement system.
- Exception: Ad-hoc purchases on corporate card require scanned receipt and manager approval within 5 business days.

Conflict of interest and gifts:
- Employees must declare any relationship with vendors during onboarding; procurement reviews conflicts.
- Gifts > $150 USD must be disclosed to People Ops and may require approval.

Section 5 — Travel & expense policy (summary and templates)
Policy highlights:
- Per diem and allowable expense categories published in Travel Guide (link in related_pages).
- Air: economy for domestic < 5 hours; business only with pre-approval for long-haul or client requirements.
- Hotels: mid-tier chain or equivalent; personal upgrades must be reimbursed by employee.
- Meals: itemized receipts required; per diem caps listed in the Travel Guide.

Expense submission template (required fields):
- Traveler name, trip purpose, dates, approver
- Itemized receipts (one receipt per line)
- Expense category (air, hotel, meals, ground)
- Business justification for any single item > $500

Fast-track approval for recurring travel:
- Sales and Solutions teams may request a travel pre-approval for quarterly customer visits; Finance will authorize an aggregated allowance and audit after quarter close.

Section 6 — Templates and forms (quick links and examples)
Included templates (copy/paste-ready):
- Access Request short form (fields): Requester | Manager | Resource | Role | Duration | Justification
- Change ticket summary (fields): Change ID | Owner | Risk | Rollback steps | Monitoring queries
- Vendor intake email: "Subject: Vendor Request — <vendor-name> — <owner>\nBody: Please find attached vendor intake form with justification, estimated annual spend, and point of contact. Requesting approval to initiate procurement."
- Expense cover note: "I confirm these expenses are business-related and comply with Redwood expense policy. Approver: <manager>"

Appendix A — Escalations and fast paths
- Critical security exposure discovered in prod: Security Pager → engage Eng SRE immediately → schedule emergency change if patch required. Post-incident, complete full RCA and update policies.
- Urgent vendor payment to avoid outage: Procurement to route emergency payment with CFO approval; document reason and reconcile within 3 business days.

Appendix B — Audit evidence & record retention
- Access requests, approvals, and provisioning logs must be retained for 7 years for regulated customers; default retention is 3 years for internal audit.
- Change tickets and rollback evidence: stored in ticketing system with attachments; retention 5 years.
- Vendor contracts: central contract repository with versioning; retention per legal guidelines.

How to get help
- Procurement & Contracts: procurement@redwood.com
- Security reviews: security-requests@redwood.com
- Access provisioning: cloudops@redwood.com
- Travel & expenses: travel@redwood.com

Revision history:
